meta.Detector: OpenCV multi-index computer vision - colour, ExG vegetation index, texture, morphology
meta.Detection classes: 19 active classes mapped to DTU Category A
meta.Annotated videos: Four MP4 files in this folder, one per clip

headlineFindings: •  The lake is the single most serious finding. Where the surface is well exposed the water is strongly eutrophic - the green algal share peaks at 99.8% and averages 51% across frames with more than 5% water in view - and the level is severely depleted, with a large rocky bed and cracked bank exposed around the footbridge.

•  Cleanliness is the weakest park-wide score. Loose ground debris covers roughly a quarter to a third of open ground in every zone, and plastic waste is visible along the lake shoreline and on the water surface.

•  Standing rain water is ponding across the children's play area - it covers around a fifth of the frame under and around the swings and slides through much of Clip 1, on ground that is already bare and compacted.
•  Ground cover is failing in the high-use zones. The children's play area is bare compacted earth; lawn cover only becomes meaningful in the nadir pass over the lake-edge greens.
•  Built assets are the strongest performer. Play equipment, open gym stations, benches, kerbs and paved pads mostly score in the 70-95% band on the paint / surface-integrity index.
•  Tree canopy is dense and vigorous across all four zones, and no stem exceeded the lean threshold for an unsafe-tree alert.
•  No encroachment or unauthorised construction was observed. One goods vehicle was detected inside the green boundary in the play-area clip.
•  No GPS telemetry (.SRT) accompanied any clip, so Category B.1 geo-tagging and the Category B.4 geo-tagged issue map could not be populated.
•  All four clips are from a single date, so Category B.3 change detection is not yet computable. This survey is the baseline.

recommendations.Finding: The lake is severely depleted and heavily eutrophic. Where open water is in view the algal share of the surface approaches 100%, and a large rocky bed with cracked, eroded bank is exposed.
recommendations.Recommended action: Commission a water-body restoration plan: de-silting, inflow and nutrient-load control, aeration, and bank stabilisation with re-profiling. Treat as the park's top capital priority.

recommendations.Finding: Floating waste is detected on the water surface and plastic waste is scattered along the shoreline and exposed bed.
recommendations.Recommended action: Deploy surface skimming or net booms at the inflow, and run a shoreline clearance drive; add bins at the bridge approach.

recommendations.Finding: Loose ground debris covers roughly a quarter to a third of open ground in every zone - the weakest park-wide score.
recommendations.Recommended action: Raise sweeping frequency across all four zones; establish a weekly leaf-fall clearance cycle and add bins where none were observed.

recommendations.Finding: The play-zone surface is predominantly bare compacted earth with no ground cover.
recommendations.Recommended action: Re-establish a wear-tolerant ground cover or install an impact-absorbing play surface; decompact and top-dress before the monsoon.

recommendations.Finding: Play and gym equipment is broadly serviceable, but several units score materially below their cluster mean on the paint-integrity index.
recommendations.Recommended action: Inspect the lowest-scoring units listed in '7. Anomalies'; sand, prime and repaint, and check all fixings, bearings and footings.

recommendations.Finding: Kerb and edging runs show breaks in continuity, and some walking-track segments score poorly on surface uniformity.
recommendations.Recommended action: Reset displaced kerb stones and patch or resurface the affected track segments.

recommendations.Finding: A goods vehicle was detected inside the green boundary.
recommendations.Recommended action: Confirm whether the movement was authorised maintenance access; otherwise enforce vehicle restrictions.

recommendations.Finding: Tree canopy is dense and vigorous throughout, and no stem exceeded the lean threshold for an unsafe-tree alert.
recommendations.Recommended action: Maintain the current arboricultural regime; no immediate intervention indicated from this pass.

recommendations.Finding: No GPS telemetry sidecar (.SRT) accompanied any of the four clips, which blocks asset geo-tagging and the geo-tagged issue map.
recommendations.Recommended action: Standardise the flight export to include the telemetry file so every detection can carry a coordinate.

recommendations.Finding: True NDVI cannot be produced from an RGB payload; the visible-band ExG proxy was used instead.
recommendations.Recommended action: Add a multispectral or red-edge payload for genuine vegetation-index monitoring.

recommendations.Finding: All four clips are single-date, so no change metric could be computed.
recommendations.Recommended action: Treat this survey as the baseline and repeat monthly on the same flight path to unlock the full Category B.3 set.

recommendations.Finding: Several framework sub-parameters (gates, signage, toilets, parking, drinking water points, dustbin fill state) were never in a field of view or are unresolvable at this altitude.
recommendations.Recommended action: Add a low-altitude amenity pass at 15-25 m over built assets so signage, bins and fixtures can be read.

recommendations.Finding: The framework proposes comparing drone imagery against sanctioned maintenance works.
recommendations.Recommended action: Supply the sanctioned works schedule and park boundary polygon to enable contractor-performance scorecards by Division, Sub-Division and Park.

categoryA.Remark: Standing dry vegetation is limited; most dry material is fallen leaf litter, logged under A4.

Proxy only - hedge edge regularity inferred from shrub blob fill ratio.
One succulent / agave bed is visible at the bridge approach but is too small and too occluded to score reliably.

Single-date capture - no prior survey to compare against.
Bare / desiccated ground taken as the dry-zone indicator.

Rain ponding on the play-area sand. Detected as open ground that is both darker and smoother than the dry ground around it. NOTE: Clips 2-4 were processed with the older, far less sensitive rule, so their counts under-report and are not comparable with Clip 1. See the detector-version note in 9. Method & Limits.
No irrigation infrastructure visible in any clip.
Inferred from tonal banding across the ground surface.
Area-based debris coverage. Discrete items on ground are not separable from sun dapple; on the water surface they ARE separable and are logged as A7 Floating Waste.
A caged bin enclosure is visible in the open-gym zone but fill state cannot be judged from above.
Scattered rubble is present on the exposed lake bank; it is logged under A7 rather than as a discrete dumping event.
Same underlying detections as the A3 Waterlogging row.
No gate in any field of view.
Kerb / edging runs detected and scored on continuity. Bridge railings are visible but not scored separately.

Recorded as the 'algal_share' field on every Water Body record (see the Detector notes column of the Detection Log) rather than as a separate box, because a standalone algal box occupies the same footprint as the water body and is removed by cross-class NMS. Peak algal share 99.8%; mean 51% across frames with more than 5% water in view.
Bright compact objects on the smooth water surface - the most reliable litter signal available.
Condition index combines algal share and turbidity proxy.
Rocky, cracked and eroded margins detected along the shoreline.
No fountain in any field of view.
Stem positions logged; informal tree belt, no formal avenue geometry.
Derived from the spread of the ExG vigour index across vegetated area.
